final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded that the disclosure, risk-acceptance, resolution, and final legal-determination gaps remain open. That means the update is a reframing of the same record, not an evidentiary change. The narrower framing is relevant in one respect: it reduces overclaiming by no longer asserting that the fraud-dispute-review gap is resolved or immaterial. But that narrowing is not enough for compliant_with_caveats, because the unresolved issue is not merely residual monitoring or documentation. It is an unresolved compliance predicate under the release policy for a named launch use case. The admissible record still shows: aggregate readiness passed and rehearsal had no severity-one incidents; the fraud-dispute-review segment misses target by 1.3 percentage points and is named in two bank pilot commitments; legal review is still open; and policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Readiness evidence supports that the system is not in general launch failure, but it does not establish that certification is policy-compliant on the present record. Because the core concern remains unresolved, the appropriate final verdict remains suspicious.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the named fraud-dispute-review limitation was disclosed before certification.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering this specific gap before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required for the named bank-pilot use case remains open.
The policy treats weaknesses affecting a contractual customer segment or named launch use case as material; the segment is named in two bank pilot commitments.
Public guidance about documenting limitations and monitoring supports governance framing but does not satisfy the internal release-policy predicate.
